passages.quote: Passive immunity provides immediate protection against infection, but that protection is temporary.
Antibodies, specifically the class of antibody referred to as IgG, are transported across the placenta.

passages.locator: Classification of Vaccines > Live, Attenuated Vaccines
passages.quote: To produce an immune response, live, attenuated vaccines must replicate in the vaccinated person.
The immune response to an inactivated vaccine is mostly antibody production. Little or no cellular immunity results.

passages.quote: Tetanus toxin interferes with the release of neurotransmitters, blocking inhibitor impulses.
In the presence of anaerobic conditions, the spores germinate.

sources.title: Pink Book, Chapter 10: Hepatitis B
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.attribution: Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). This material is also available from CDC at no charge. No CDC or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: Persons who respond to HepB vaccine are positive only for anti-HBs.
Persons who recover from natural HBV infection are typically positive for both anti-HBs and anti-HBc.
IgM anti-HBc appears in persons with acute disease about the time of illness onset and indicates recent infection with HBV.
HBeAg is a marker that is associated with a high number of infective HBV particles in the serum and a higher risk of infectivity.

sources.title: How Flu Viruses Can Change: Drift and Shift
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.attribution: Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). This material is also available from CDC at no charge. No CDC or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: Drift consists of small changes (or mutations) in the genes of influenza viruses that can lead to changes in the surface proteins of the virus.
Shift is an abrupt, major change in a flu A virus, resulting in new HA and/or new HA and NA proteins.

passages.quote: The covalent linkage renders the otherwise T-cell independent polysaccharide antigen to become T-cell dependent thus inducing long term immunity.

sources.title: Definition and Facts of Adrenal Insufficiency and Addison's Disease
sources.publisher: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.attribution: Source: NIDDK, National Institutes of Health. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.locator: What is adrenal insufficiency? > Secondary adrenal insufficiency
passages.quote: If the pituitary doesn’t make enough ACTH, the adrenal glands don’t make enough cortisol.

passages.locator: Who is more likely to develop adrenal insufficiency?
passages.quote: People who take glucocorticoid medicines, such as prednisone, for a long time and then stop are most likely to develop tertiary adrenal insufficiency.

sources.title: Treatment for Adrenal Insufficiency and Addison's Disease
sources.publisher: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.attribution: Source: NIDDK, National Institutes of Health. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.locator: How do doctors treat adrenal insufficiency?
passages.quote: Treatment for adrenal crisis includes immediate IV injections of corticosteroids and large amounts of IV saline, a salt solution, with dextrose added.

sources.publisher: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sources.attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: ALD signals your kidneys to release more sodium into your blood and to get rid of potassium through urine.

passages.quote: Nephrotic syndrome usually happens when the glomeruli are damaged, allowing too much protein to leak from the blood into the urine.
high levels of cholesterol and other lipids (fats) in your blood, called hyperlipidemia

sources.title: Type 1 Diabetes
sources.publisher: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.attribution: Source: NIDDK, National Institutes of Health. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: Type 1 diabetes develops when the body’s immune system destroys the cells in the pancreas that make insulin. These cells are called beta cells.

passages.locator: What health problems can people with type 1 diabetes develop? > Diabetic ketoacidosis
passages.quote: Your body will begin to use fat as a source of energy instead. This process produces substances called ketones.

sources.title: The A1C Test and Diabetes
sources.publisher: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.attribution: Source: NIDDK, National Institutes of Health. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: The A1C test measures the amount of hemoglobin with attached glucose and reflects your average blood glucose levels over the past 3 months.

sources.title: What Is Sickle Cell Disease?
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
sources.attribution: Source: NHLBI, National Institutes of Health. No NIH or U.S. Government endorsement is implied.

passages.quote: When red blood cells sickle, they do not bend or move easily and can block blood flow to the rest of the body.

passages.quote: In a family where both parents are carriers and do not have the disease, roughly a quarter of their children will inherit two disease-causing alleles and have the disease.
